strongest_angle: Examine how the 2026 super El Niño shattered temperature records in the Pacific Ocean months ahead of its December peak, reaching 3.08 degrees Celsius warmer than the 1991 to 2020 average according to Science News and the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

key_facts.fact: On September 21, 2026, the daily sea surface temperature in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean reached 3.08 degrees Celsius warmer than the 1991 to 2020 average, as reported by Science News.
The Copernicus Climate Change Service stated that sea surface temperatures in a key region of the Pacific reached 29.70 degrees Celsius in September 2026.
Australia's Bureau of Meteorology reported that the weekly relative Niño3.4 index reached a record +2.88 degrees Celsius for the week ending October 25, 2026.
